newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian employers told to prevent sexual harassment.
newsitem.headline: Indian employers told to prevent sexual harassment.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Wednesday ordered employers to prevent sexual harassment in the workplace in a far-reaching ruling that judges said aimed to plug a gap in the nation's legal framework.

The three-judge bench, ruling on a written petition seeking equality between the two genders, said all employers in the private and public sectors "should take appropriate steps to prevent sexual harassment", and issued a detailed set of guidelines to be followed.

The 24-page ruling said employers must expressly prohibit "physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; sexually coloured remarks; showing pornography or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature".
It said government employers should inflict appropriate penalties to punish offenders.

The judges said employers must ensure "there is no hostile environment towards women at (the) workplace and no employee woman should have reasonable grounds to believe that she is disadvantaged in connection with her employment".
Victims of sexual harassment must have the option of seeking either the transfer of the offender or their own transfer, the ruling said.
A committee to hear workplace complaints should be headed by a woman, and at least half its members should be female.
The bench said it was issuing the order "in the absence of (a) domestic law occupying the field".
The Supreme Court has taken the lead in a number of social issues, including efforts to combat corruption among civil servants and politicians.
